adbartf: Choice-letter key (A/B = true/false) but the option list/order is not in the export. The statement's truth was derived independently from the bar values, yet the keyed letter is not a function of it (both letters occur for true and for false statements): option order is shuffled per question and cannot be reconstructed, so the key cannot be verified.
akprim: Choice-letter key. The stem 'Which of these is primary/secondary data?' carries no content; the four candidate options are not in the export, so neither the content nor the letter can be checked.
avstatq: Choice-letter key. The options are not exported; the keyed letter varies with the topic (params[0]) but not with the item form (statistical question / single-case question / statement), so the classification behind each letter cannot be reconstructed from the stem. Unverifiable.
akmex: Choice-letter key. Mutual exclusivity/exhaustiveness of A and B was derived by enumeration, but the keyed letter is not a function of it (options shuffled per question, option texts not exported), so the key cannot be verified.
akscale: Choice-letter key. The probability of the event was derived by enumeration (0, in (0,1/2), 1/2, in (1/2,1), 1), but the keyed letter takes every value within one category (options shuffled per question, option texts not exported): key cannot be verified.
akssl: Choice-letter key. The stem asks which listed sample space / event set is correct; the candidate lists are not in the export, so the key cannot be checked.
anaxiom: Choice-letter key. The stem asks which assignment of probabilities to omega1..omega4 is valid; the four assignments are not in the export (the stem is identical for all 300 questions), so nothing can be checked.
anvalid: Choice-letter key. The stem asks which of four numbers cannot be a probability; the four numbers are not in the export (the stem is identical for all questions), so nothing can be checked.
atvtype: Choice-letter key. The stem asks which listed quantity/vector type is correct; the options are not in the export, so nothing can be checked.
anavgav: Choice-letter key; option texts not exported. The true category was derived exactly (claimed overall mean right / true mean above the claim / below) and the keyed letter is a single-valued function of it over all 300 questions (A=right 67, B=true mean above 123, C=true mean below 110, see choice_consistency.json), i.e. internally consistent, but the letter->option wording is not exported, so the key is not independently verified.
anstack: Choice-letter key; option texts not exported. The larger 100%-stacked 'walk' share was derived exactly from the bars; the letter is a single-valued function of it over all 300 questions (A = Class 9A larger 158, B = 9B larger 140, C = equal 2), consistent with the natural option order, but the option wording is not exported, so the key is not independently verified.
atcv: Choice-letter key; option texts not exported. Coefficients of variation were compared exactly; the letter is a single-valued function of the result over all 300 questions (A = first named more consistent 103, B = second 99, C = equal 98), consistent with the natural option order, but the option wording is not exported, so the key is not independently verified.
aqrank: Choice-letter key; option texts not exported. The number of solutions was derived from exact ranks of A and [A|b]; the letter is a single-valued function of it over all 400 questions (A unique 133, B infinitely many 129, C none 138), but the option wording is not exported, so the key is not independently verified.
ansure: Choice-letter key; option texts not exported. Sure/impossible/neither was derived by enumeration of the sample space; the letter is a single-valued function of it over all 118 questions (A impossible 31, B sure 28, C neither 59), but the option wording is not exported, so the key is not independently verified.
atindt: Choice-letter key; option texts not exported. Independence and mutual exclusivity of A and B were derived by enumeration; the letter is a single-valued function of the pair over all 400 questions (A independent 121, B dependent and mutually exclusive 144, C dependent and not exclusive 135), but the option wording is not exported, so the key is not independently verified.
asmex: Choice-letter key; option texts not exported. Mutual exclusivity and exhaustiveness of A and B were derived by enumeration; the letter is a single-valued function of the pair over all 320 questions (A exclusive-not-exhaustive, B exhaustive-not-exclusive, C both, D neither, 80 each), but the option wording is not exported, so the key is not independently verified.
